corridor.description: Brazilian nationals benefit from the CPLP facilitation agreement (Acordo sobre Mobilidade entre os Estados-membros da CPLP) with Portugal, which provides a simplified pathway to long-stay residence. The primary route for employees is the CPLP residence visa (Visto de Residencia CPLP), followed by an AIMA appointment in Portugal. The D2 (self-employed/entrepreneur) and D7 (passive income/retired) visas are secondary routes.

primary_sources.title: Residence Visa documentation -- Portuguese MFA Consular Portal
AIMA -- Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum (Portugal)

pathways.duration_basis: Initial residence authorisation valid 1 year; renewable for 2+2 years; after 5 years eligible for permanent residence.

eligibility.salary_basis: No statutory minimum; salary must support self-sufficiency

pathways.duration_basis: 4-month entry visa, converted to residence authorisation at AIMA.
4-month entry visa, converted to residence authorisation at AIMA.

eligibility.income_basis: Equal to or above the Portuguese minimum wage (2026)

required_documents.document_name: Valid Brazilian passport (biometric, minimum 6 months validity beyond intended stay)
Residence visa application form (Type D, CPLP -- signed and dated)
CPLP consular visa request -- formal declaration invoking the CPLP mobility agreement
required_documents.description: Brazilian nationals must explicitly invoke the CPLP Mobility Agreement at the Portuguese consulate to access the simplified CPLP residence pathway. Typically a cover letter referencing the Acordo sobre Mobilidade CPLP, exempting them from quota restrictions that apply to other third-country nationals.

required_documents.document_name: Proof of accommodation in Portugal (lease agreement, property deed, or employer-provided housing letter)
Health insurance covering the full visa validity period
Brazilian birth certificate + criminal record certificate (apostille from Cartorio brasileiro)
required_documents.translation_notes: Portuguese is the official language in Brazil; no translation required. Hague Apostille must be issued by a Brazilian notary (Cartorio).

required_documents.document_name: Business plan for self-employed / entrepreneur D2 visa applicants
required_documents.description: The D2 visa requires a detailed business plan demonstrating the viability of the self-employed activity or entrepreneurial project in Portugal. The plan should include: business description, market analysis, financial projections (3 years), evidence of investment capacity, and expected job creation.

required_documents.document_name: Proof of passive income for D7 visa (pension statement, dividends, rental income -- minimum EUR 820/month in 2026)
required_documents.description: D7 applicants must demonstrate regular passive income sufficient for self-sufficiency in Portugal. Accepted sources: pension statements, rental income certificates, dividend statements. Brazilian documents require apostille; translation not required (Portuguese language shared).

required_documents.document_name: Long-stay visa processing timeline and steps for BR-PT CPLP route
required_documents.description: The BR to PT long-stay visa (CPLP residence) processing steps: (1) Book consular appointment at Portuguese Consulado in Brazil -- wait 1 to 8 weeks depending on city; (2) Submit full dossier at appointment; (3) Consulate processes visa -- 30 to 90 days; (4) Enter Portugal with Type D visa; (5) Book AIMA appointment within 90 days of arrival; (6) AIMA issues residence authorisation card. Total elapsed time from booking to residence card: typically 3 to 6 months.

post_arrival_steps.name: Book and attend AIMA appointment to obtain residence authorisation card
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Long-stay visa (Type D) is valid for 4 months; residence authorisation must be requested within this period.
post_arrival_steps.where: AIMA -- Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum (online booking at aima.gov.pt or via Loja do Cidadao)

post_arrival_steps.name: Obtain Portuguese NIF (Numero de Identificacao Fiscal -- tax number)
post_arrival_steps.deadline_basis: Required before opening a bank account, signing a lease, or registering with AIMA in person. Can be obtained before arrival via Portuguese consulate in Brazil.
post_arrival_steps.where: AT -- Autoridade Tributaria e Aduaneira (tax office) or Portuguese consulate in Brazil

path_classifier_rules.rationale: Default CPLP facilitation route for Brazilian nationals seeking salaried employment in Portugal.
Self-employed Brazilians and entrepreneurs use the D2 visa with business plan.
Retired Brazilians and passive income holders use the D7 visa.

known_gaps: CPLP agreement terms are subject to renegotiation; verify validity at next_review_due.
Portuguese-Brazilian Treaty of Friendship special status (after 3 years) is not encoded as a downstream pathway.
NHR (Non-Habitual Resident) tax regime for income optimization is out of scope.
AIMA appointment wait times vary significantly by region; real-time availability not tracked.
